## Reference Rivers

-   79 catchments all over Norway

-   Water chemistry sampled monthly 2017-2022

    ```{r}
    # Load libraries
    library(tidyverse)
    library(sf)
    library(terra)
    library(units)
    library(raster)
    library(rgeos)
    library(tmap)
    library(RColorBrewer)

    # delineated watersheds
    watershed70 <- read_sf("Raw_Data/Shape_files/catchment_delineation/RefElv.shp") 

    # river station coordinates
    stations <- read_csv("Raw_Data/Shape_files/Refelv_Station_Coordinates.csv") 
    stations_cord <- st_as_sf(stations, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = "WGS84", remove = FALSE)
    stations_cord = st_transform(stations_cord, "EPSG:25833")

    # Interactive map
    tmap_mode(mode = c("view")) # Set for interactive viewing. 

    tmap_options(check.and.fix = TRUE) 

    tm <- tm_shape(watershed70) + 
       tm_borders() +
      tm_shape(stations_cord) +
        tm_dots(size = 0.05, id = "site_name")

    tm
    ```

## Next Steps II: Drought impacts on water chemistry

1.  **Drought impacts on water chemistry:**

hypotheses following discussions with Jan-Erik, Øyvind Garmo, Heleen & Francois:

-   **Temperature:** increased water temperatures expected during drought. or, alternatively, decreased temperatures due to increased ground water contribution.

-   **Acidity:** Expected acid pulse following periods of drought due to production of acidity (from oxidation of reduced S) in catchment soils, which will be flushed out post-drought.

-   **Nutrients:** increased retention in the catchment. Given lower loads, the river will be more nutrient limited.

-   **DOC/water color:** Reduced DOC and water color following drought, and higher aromaticity of DOC.

-   **Ions:** Increased ions following drought (e.g. ca usually higher in winter due to more ground water and less surface flow)

-   **Metals:** Increased concentrations following drought if acidic pulse present.

2.  **Differences between dry and wet years among land cover types:**

hypothesis 1: Drought impacts water chemistry differently depending on elevation, forest cover, presence of bogs, ect.

hypothesis 2: catchment and riparian zone characteristics have lower predictive power during drought years due to reduced connectivity.
